Evidence source: Vault/30-Experiments/EXP-20261005-001 - Thumper transplanted into Moonlit Cliffs.md

## Where Thumper lives (static, PC)

- **Type 16 is Thumper.** Character loader `0x00445020` switches on each pool
  slot's type; case `0x10` pushes `"chars2\thumper"` (`0x004DDEF0`,
  referenced at `0x0044531F`). Case `0x1D` (29) is `chars3\molt`, so the
  Battle Arena "grasshopper" in [[PC original level Blender maps]] is Molt, not
  Thumper.
- **One native placement:** Council Chamber (engine 2, `LEVEL02/LEVEL.RAW`),
  type-35 slot 1, script 9, stored (141, −1857, 101). Its native floor below
  is 1693.5, so he starts 3,550 units above it
  (`original-levels/03-council-chamber/original-map.json`).
- **The RAW pair is the disc files.** Council Chamber's 0x101/0x102 packets
  whose second dword is 16 equal `CD/CHARS2/THUMPER.ANM` (34,304 B) and
  `THUMPER.ALL` (11,804 B) after their 8-byte heads, byte for byte. All 174
  model faces use texture page 21; page 21 is absent from Moonlit's RAW. A
  render of it shows grasshopper skin, eyes and claws.


## Hardware arm 1 (classic selector, null sink, controllers disabled)

`make session-audit` clean before launch. Game PID 218674 under gamescope
218308; 6/6 hardware markers, no software markers.

- **Load:** `bugs.log` shows `LOAD : Loading file R:\PC\BUGS\cd\chars2\thumper.anm`
  then `.all`. Nothing else requested them; the type byte did.
- **Spawn:** slot 10 read type 16, health 50, flags 0x52, script PC
  `0x004C7EE8`. The enemy total read 11 (10 + Thumper).
- **Berry:** walking onto the purple berry right of the spawn set
  `0x0059D9A7` to 4. It survived three deaths and reset to 0 only on level
  re-entry (EXP-20260818-004's selector).
- **Wake and drop:** when Flik approached, Thumper fell from −6766 to about
  the ground (−3192), flags became 0x4053/0x5053/0x1053, PC `0x004C7F02`.
  He chased Flik, cornered him against the valley wall and killed him four
  times. Frames show the tall grasshopper with spiky legs and wings, textured,
  dimmed by Moonlit's night light, and a purple splash on hits.
- **Damage:** 28 health changes between samples: 27 of −3 and one −6 (two
  hits). Health 50 → 32 → 11, then 38 → 32 → 26 → 11 → 0 in the second visit.
  His health persisted across Flik's deaths; level re-entry reset him.
- **Death:** at 0 his slot read type 0, health 0, flags 0x18D1 (0x880 set),
  respawn 0, PC `0x004C7F6A`. The game ran 10 s more with no fault in
  `launch.log`, and he did not return.
- **Lives:** before the fight Flik was once back at the spawn with health
  refilled (cause not sampled; a spider was beside him). The first in-fight
  death then ended the game (back to the Flik's Journey select). In the second
  visit three deaths respawned him in-level. Not investigated.
- **Model records:** `0x005A9660` entries were used up to index 200 of 300;
  the overflow flag `0x005C5960` read 0.
- Closed through the packet; audit clean. Log moved to `arm1/bugs.log`.


## Static audit of the dependencies (research subagent, disassembly)

Confirmed from instructions or data unless marked:

- **Script 9** (`0x004C7EE8`..`0x004C7F08`): frame sequence, a blocking fall
  (op6, mode 4) that spawns dust type 1 on landing, op11 subroutine 4
  (`0x00431C90`: `[0x0059EF70] = 60`, read only by `0x00431CB0`), then a loop
  of random waits and random targets around home. Nothing reads the engine.
- **Handler `0x0041C100`** only plays looping sound row 0x1A (sample 31,
  `WASPBUZZ.WAV`, present in banks 1–18). No damage either way.
- **The boss fight is engine-2 code.** Per-frame dispatcher `0x00418780`
  (table `0x004187E8`, called at `0x004145BB` with `[0x00861C84]`) sends
  engine 2 to `0x00431CB0`; init dispatcher `0x00418690` sends it to
  `0x00431BF0`. `0x00431CB0` reads slot 1 (`0x0059B6AC`) and slots 2/3. It
  plays hit voices, makes slot 2 or 3 his thrown projectile, and below
  health 21 runs a camera cut, script 13 and `[0x0059A5B0] = 1` (level won).
  The HUD health bar (`0x00416890`, at `0x0041725A`) also draws only in
  engine 2. Engine 1's routines are `0x004317D0`/`0x00431730`.
- **Damage** is `0x00429790`: purple −3, gold −4, blue and green −2; red is
  deflected because flag 0x40 is set. Health is record +0x6E from source
  +0x10 (50). At ≤ 0 he takes the ordinary kill path and, with source
  +0x11 = 0, is not respawned.
- **Sprites:** engine 1 and engine 2 copy byte-identical 50-descriptor sprite
  tables (`0x004DA6B0`, `0x004DA7B8`), so no effect on his path is missing.
- **RAW pair (inferred, strong):** `0x00465030` has no 0x101/0x102 case and
  no instruction compares against those tags; the loader reads the disc
  files. The pair is kept for parity with Moonlit's other creature types.
- **Do not use slots 25 or 63:** engine 1's update writes through slot 25
  (Dot) unchecked, and level start special-cases slot 63.


## Contradiction (recorded, not resolved)

The static audit says homing selection `0x00428400` needs flags bit 0x0001,
which 0x0052 lacks, so green/purple homing "never" picks Thumper. At runtime
his flags were 0x4053/0x5053/0x1053 after waking, which have bit 0x0001.
Purple hits landed, but no arm instrumented whether a shot homed.
**Discriminating experiment:** with Thumper awake and no other enemy near,
sample the projectile's target pointer +0x10 and flag +0x33 bit 0x08 after a
purple throw.

*Later (2026-10-05):* [[EXP-20261005-002 - Native bosses and tough enemies in Moonlit Cliffs]]
saw bit 0x0001 appear on every boss once awake. Airborne bosses (1,974 and
2,304 up) took purple hits, and a frame shows a berry climbing toward the
flying Hopper. That supports lock-on; the projectile sample is still not taken.


## Confirmed, inferred, unknown

- **Confirmed (static + runtime):** a type-35 row brings its character model
  by type; Thumper loads, renders, wakes, fights, takes −3 per purple hit,
  dies and is removed in Moonlit without a crash.
- **Confirmed (static):** the boss behaviour, health bar and win are not in
  the row; they are engine-2 code bound to slot 1.
- **Inferred:** the 0x101/0x102 packets are unused on PC.
- **Unknown:** whether his sound plays (null sink); homing lock-on; behaviour
  near cliffs or other enemies; a gold kill's enemy-counter effect; the
  user's play.
